judge.reason: The answer names all four requirements and says what each one asks of charge. It validates the amount (R-CHARGE-AMOUNT), returns the first receipt when a retry uses the same key (R-IDEMPOTENT-CHARGE), lets a declined charge be retried (R-CHARGE-DECLINE), and records an audit entry (R-AUDIT-MONEY). The amount and audit descriptions are thin, but they still state the requirement and give the ID, so q1–q4 are true. For the tests, the answer mostly paraphrases instead of naming them. "Appending an audit entry" is almost the exact test name `appends an audit entry`, so q5 is true. "Retrying without a second gateway charge" and "retrying after a decline" describe tests but don't give their names, so q6 and q7 are false. "Receipts used for refunds" does not name `refunds to the original transaction`, so q8 is false. "Two validateAmount tests" does not name either amount test, so q9 and q10 are false.

finalMessage:
[`Processor.charge`](/tmp/ostf-trials/phase5/codex.rules.ts-shop.T1.3/repo/src/payments.ts:83) is the shop’s payment entry point. Checkout calls it to charge an account through the gateway. It validates the amount, returns the first receipt for a retry with the same key, rejects a reused key with different charge details, allows a declined charge to be retried, and records a successful charge and audit entry. [`REQUIREMENTS.md`](/tmp/ostf-trials/phase5/codex.rules.ts-shop.T1.3/repo/REQUIREMENTS.md:61) ties those behaviors to R-IDEMPOTENT-CHARGE, R-CHARGE-AMOUNT, R-CHARGE-DECLINE, R-AUDIT-MONEY, and D-IDEMPOTENCY-STORE.

The direct tests in [`src/payments.test.ts`](/tmp/ostf-trials/phase5/codex.rules.ts-shop.T1.3/repo/src/payments.test.ts:32) cover retrying without a second gateway charge, rejecting a reused key with another amount, retrying after a decline, and appending an audit entry. Two `validateAmount` tests cover the amount bounds that `charge` enforces. Checkout and refund tests also exercise `charge` indirectly through order placement, declined checkout, and receipts used for refunds.
